title: Astigmatism, Reading of Spectacle Prescription and Binocular Errors

questions.q: Astigmatism overview per p130:
opts: Cylindrical error; different power in the two principal meridians
Spherical refractive error with same power in both principal axes
A retinal disease of the macular photoreceptors
Only a disorder of the crystalline lens
questions.exp: Cylindrical refractory error; different refractory power in both principal meridians/axes of eye (in spherical errors same power in both axes). (Book p130)

questions.q: Match regular astigmatism types per p130 — 1) With the rule 2) Against the rule 3) Oblique … A) Horizontal meridian more curved B) Vertical meridian more curved C) Principal meridians perpendicular but not at 90° and 180°
questions.exp: With the rule: vertical meridian more curved; against the rule: horizontal meridian more curved; oblique: perpendicular but not at 90°/180°. (Book p130)

questions.q: Irregular astigmatism per p130:
opts: Both principal meridians remain perfectly perpendicular
Meridians not perpendicular; eg corneal scar, cataract
Corrected fully by a spherical lens
questions.exp: Irregular: both principal meridians are not perpendicular; can be due to pathologies eg corneal scar, cataract, etc. (Book p130)

questions.q: Match refractive types per p130 — 1) Simple myopic 2) Compound myopic 3) Simple hypermetropic 4) Mixed … A) Both axes myopic B) Axis 1 emmetropic, axis 2 myopic C) Axis 1 emmetropic, axis 2 hypermetropic D) One axis myopic, other hypermetropic
questions.exp: Simple myopic emmetropic+myopic; compound myopic both myopic; simple hypermetropic emmetropic+hypermetropic; compound hypermetropic both hypermetropic; mixed myopic+hypermetropic. (Book p130)

questions.q: All pairs are correctly matched per p130 EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Compound hypermetropic = both axes hypermetropic; both axes myopic = compound myopic. (Book p130)

questions.q: Clinical features of astigmatism per p130:
opts: Loss of sharpness (all letters seem to stretch/merge) and asthenopia
questions.exp: 1 Loss of vision: loss of sharpness (all letters seem to stretch/merge); 2 asthenopia. (Book p130)

questions.q: In spherical refractory errors per p130:
questions.exp: In spherical refractory errors → same power in both axes. (Book p130)

questions.q: The two principal meridians/axes of the eye per p130 diagram are:
questions.exp: Vertical meridian (Vp) and horizontal meridian (Hp) are the axes of eye. (Book p130)

questions.q: Cylindrical lens power orientation per p131:
questions.exp: Cylindrical lenses have power 90° to their axis; only 1 axis has power. (Book p131)

questions.q: Match per p131 — 1) Plano convex cylinder 2) Plano concave cylinder 3) Toric contact lens … A) For myopic astigmatism B) For hypermetropic astigmatism C) A lens with 2 surfaces with different powers
questions.exp: Plano convex for hypermetropic A; plano concave for myopic A; toric contact lens = lens with 2 surfaces with different powers. (Book p131)

questions.q: Sturm's conoid per p131 is:
opts: Arrangement of light rays refracted through a toric surface
questions.exp: Sturm's conoid: arrangement of light rays refracted through a toric surface. (Book p131)

questions.q: In Sturm's conoid per p131 (Vc > Hc), the intermediate focal point D corresponds to:
questions.exp: B vertical rays focussed; D circle of least diffusion (convergence of horizontal rays = divergence of vertical rays); F horizontal rays focussed. (Book p131)

questions.q: Principle of astigmatic correction per p131:
opts: Circle of least diffusion placed on retina → clear image
Focusses the vertical rays exactly on the retina for clarity
Focusses the horizontal rays exactly on the retina
Diverges all rays equally in both meridians
questions.exp: Principle: converges rays so circle of least diffusion lies at retina → clear image visualized. (Book p131)

questions.q: Per p131, Vc > Hc leads to all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Vc > Hc → Vp > Hp; vertical rays focussed (B), then circle of least diffusion (D), then horizontal rays focussed (F). (Book p131)

questions.q: A toric contact lens per p131 has:
questions.exp: Toric contact lens: a lens with 2 surfaces with different powers. (Book p131)

questions.q: Astigmatism LASIK per p132:
opts: Selective burning off of the axis with higher curvature in the cornea
questions.exp: Astigmatism LASIK: selective burning off of the axis with higher curvature in the cornea; also accurate keratotomy and LRI (limbal relaxing incisions). (Book p132)

questions.q: Match astigmatism surgery per p132 — 1) Astigmatism LASIK 2) Accurate keratotomy 3) LRI … A) Limbal relaxing incisions B) Selective ablation of steeper corneal axis C) Precise corneal cutting procedure
questions.exp: Astigmatism LASIK selective burning of higher curvature axis; accurate keratotomy; LRI = limbal relaxing incisions; shared principle: partial thickness incision → heals by fibrosis → vertical curvature stretched → reduced Vc. (Book p132)

questions.q: LRI principle in with-the-rule astigmatism (Vc > Hc) per p132:
opts: Partial thickness incision at 90° and 180° on cornea/limbus → heals by fibrosis → vertical curvature stretched → reduced Vc
No fibrosis occurs after the incisions
Incisions placed at 45° oblique meridians only
questions.exp: With the rule (Vc > Hc): partial thickness incision at 90° and 180° on cornea/limbus → heals by fibrosis → vertical curvature stretched → reduced Vc. (Book p132)

questions.q: Match prescription columns per p132 — 1) Sph 2) Cyl 3) (+) power 4) (-) power … A) For astigmatism B) For myopia/hypermetropia C) Prescribed for hypermetropia D) Prescribed for myopia
questions.exp: RE right eye; LE left eye; Sph spherical power for myopia/hypermetropia; Cyl cylindrical power for astigmatism; (+) for hypermetropia; (-) for myopia. (Book p132)

questions.q: Match lens type per p132 table — 1) Myopia 2) Simple myopic astigmatism 3) Compound myopic astigmatism 4) Mixed astigmatism … A) - sph B) - cyl C) - sph/- cyl D) - sph/+ cyl (or + sph/- cyl)
questions.exp: Myopia - sph; simple myopic A - cyl; compound myopic A - sph/- cyl; hypermetropia + sph; simple hypermetropic A + cyl; compound hypermetropic A + sph/+ cyl; mixed - sph/+ cyl or + sph/- cyl. (Book p132)

questions.q: Example prescription for compound hypermetropic astigmatism per p132:
questions.exp: Compound hypermetropic astigmatism: + sph/+ cyl, example +0.5D sph/+1 D cyl. (Book p132)

questions.q: RE and LE in a spectacle prescription per p132 mean:
questions.exp: RE: right eye; LE: left eye. (Book p132)

questions.q: Simple transformation per p133 is done to ensure:
questions.exp: Simple transformation done to ensure that cyl power > sph power. (Book p133)

questions.q: Simple transformation rules per p133: new sph = old sph + old cyl; new cyl = -(old cyl); new axis = ___.
questions.exp: New axis: perpendicular to old axis. (Book p133)

questions.q: A prescription reads -x D sph /+y D cyl @180° with x > y per p133. After simple transformation it becomes:
questions.exp: New sph = old sph + old cyl; new cyl = -(old cyl); new axis perpendicular → (y-x) D sph/-y D cyl @90°. (Book p133)

questions.q: Match per p133 table (C = convex, V = concave) — 1) With the rule, axis 180° 2) With the rule, axis 90° 3) Against the rule, axis 180° 4) Against the rule, axis 90° … A) - lens (C) B) + lens (V) C) + lens (V) D) - lens (C)
questions.exp: With the rule: 180° - lens (C), 90° + lens (V); against the rule: 180° + lens (V), 90° - lens (C). (Book p133)

questions.q: -1D cyl @180° per p133 gives:
opts: ↑ Power at 90° → vertical power > horizontal power → with the rule astigmatism
questions.exp: Power of cylindrical lens is perpendicular to its axis → ↑ power at 90° → vertical power > horizontal power: with the rule astigmatism. (Book p133)

questions.q: Power of a cylindrical lens lies per p133:
questions.exp: Power of cylindrical lens is perpendicular to its axis. (Book p133)

questions.q: Aniseikonia per p133:
opts: Different shape (distortion) and/or size of an image between both eyes d/t varying thickness of glasses
Same image size perceived in both eyes
Only a colour difference between the eyes
Diplopia caused by extraocular muscle palsy
questions.exp: Different shape (distortion) and/or size of an image between both eyes; occurs d/t varying thickness of glasses (convex thicker at center, concave thick at periphery). (Book p133)

questions.q: Match distortion defects per p133 — 1) Pin cushion defect 2) Barrel defect … A) Seen with high minus (-) correction B) Seen with very high plus (+) correction
questions.exp: Pin cushion defect with very high plus (+) correction; barrel defect with high minus (-) correction. (Book p133)

questions.q: Anisometropia per p134 is significant if the difference is:
questions.exp: Different refractory power b/w both eyes; significant if difference >2.5 D. (Book p134)

questions.q: Magnification rule for convex lenses per p134:
questions.exp: Magnification rule for convex lenses: for 1 D → 2% image magnification. (Book p134)

questions.q: Significant anisometropia per p134 leads to:
opts: Varying image sizes → failure to fuse → diplopia; Rx surgery
The brain fuses the two different sized images without symptoms
No symptoms at all in either eye
questions.exp: If significant anisometropia: varying sizes of images from each eye → failure to fuse images → diplopia; Rx: surgical correction. (Book p134)
